grc:other:Ι.gloss: The upper case letter iota, a letter resp. the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

grc:other:ι.gloss: Lower-case iota (ἰῶτα), the ninth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the close front unrounded vowel /i/. It is preceded by θ and followed by κ.

grc:other:-κτόνος.gloss: -cidal; added to nouns to form an adjective indicating a killing agent for the first noun

grc:verb:εὐαγγελίζω.gloss: to bring or announce good news

grc:verb:λέγω.gloss: to put in order, arrange, gather

grc:verb:δέομαι.gloss: present mediopassive indicative first-person singular of δέω (déō, “to tie; to need”)

grc:name:Συράκουσαι.gloss: Syracuse (a city and port in Sicily; an ancient Doric city-state in Magna Graecia)

grc:art:ὀ.gloss: Cretan and Lesbian form of ὁ (ho, “the”)

grc:pron:ὀ.gloss: Cretan and Lesbian form of ὁ (ho, demonstrative pronoun)

grc:pron:ὄ.gloss: Cretan and Lesbian form of ὅ (hó, relative pronoun)

grc:name:Σικελία.gloss: Sicily (an island and former kingdom in Europe)

grc:part:μέν.gloss: on the one hand (answered by δέ)

grc:part:οὐχ.gloss: alternative form of οὐ (ou), used before a vowel with rough breathing

grc:pron:τῆς.gloss: feminine genitive singular of ὁ (ho, demonstrative pronoun) and ὅ (hó, relative pronoun)

grc:name:Γαῖα.gloss: Gaia or Gaea, the Earth personified as a goddess

grc:verb:γνώσονται.gloss: third-person plural future active indicative of γιγνώσκω (gignṓskō)

grc:part:ἄν.gloss: (particle marking contingency; no single English equivalent)

grc:pron:ἐγών.gloss: Epic and Doric form of ἐγώ (egṓ, “I”)

grc:pron:νώ.gloss: we two; both of us; us two

grc:part:τοι.gloss: let me tell you; you see; certainly (a discourse particle which assures the listener that what the speaker says is true, or that the listener knows it is true)

grc:name:Ζεύξιππος.gloss: a male given name, equivalent to English Zeuxippus

grc:pron:ἡ.gloss: masculine/neuter genitive singular of ὁ (ho, demonstrative pronoun)

grc:pron:ἁ.gloss: masculine/neuter genitive singular of ὁ (ho, demonstrative pronoun)

grc:verb:ἐστί.gloss: third-person singular present active indicative of εἰμί (eimí)

grc:verb:ἔστιν.gloss: paroxytone third-person singular present indicative active of εἰμί (eimí) with movable nu

grc:noun:εὐθεῖα.gloss: ellipsis of εὐθεῖα πτῶσις (eutheîa ptôsis, “nominative case”, literally “straight case”)

grc:pron:ταῖς.gloss: feminine dative plural of ὁ (ho, demonstrative pronoun) and ὅ (hó, relative pronoun)

grc:name:Ἀρίσταρχος.gloss: a male given name, equivalent to English Aristarchus

grc:verb:εἰρημένος.gloss: perfect mediopassive participle of εἴρω (eírō, “say, speak, tell”)

grc:noun:μέσῳ.gloss: dative singular of μέσος (mésos) and μέσον (méson)

grc:conj:ὥστε.gloss: so that, with the result that

grc:adv:ὥστε.gloss: so that, with the result that

grc:prep:καθ'.gloss: apocopic form of κᾰτᾰ́ (kătắ) (used before a rough breathing)

grc:pron:τοιοῦτος.gloss: of this sort or kind, such

grc:other:Γ.gloss: The letter gamma (γάμμα), the third letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:adv:μάλιστα.gloss: most, most of all, above all

grc:verb:φαίνεται.gloss: third-person singular present mediopassive indicative of φαίνω (phaínō)

grc:verb:ποιεῖται.gloss: third-person singular present mediopassive indicative contracted of ποιέω (poiéō)

grc:verb:γένοιτο.gloss: third-person singular aorist middle optative of γίγνομαι (gígnomai)

grc:other:τ.gloss: to be in motion together with

grc:other:Τ.gloss: The letter tau (ταῦ), the 19th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:verb:ἐών.gloss: Epic and Ionic form of ὤν (ṓn): present participle of εἰμῐ́ (eimĭ́)

grc:other:λ.gloss: Lower-case lambda (λάβδα), the 11th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the alveolar lateral approximant /l/. It is preceded by κ and followed by μ.

grc:other:δ.gloss: Lower case delta (δέλτα), the fourth letter of Greek alphabet. It represented in Ancient Greek a voiced dental plosive: /d/ and in modern Greek a voiced dental fricative: /ð/. It is preceded by γ and followed by ε.

grc:other:Δ.gloss: The letter delta (δέλτα (délta)), the fourth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:name:Φειδίας.gloss: a male given name, Pheidias and Phidias

grc:adj:ἁμός.gloss: ἁμός (A) or ἀμός [α], ή , όν , Aeol. ἄμμος A, No.

grc:name:Πατήρ.gloss: God the Father; (one of the three Persons of the Trinity)

grc:verb:ᾖ.gloss: third-person singular present active subjunctive of εἰμί (eimí)

grc:adj:μέγιστος.gloss: superlative degree of μέγᾰς (mégăs): biggest; largest

grc:part:οὐκ.gloss: alternative form of οὐ (ou), used before a vowel with smooth breathing

grc:verb:δέω.gloss: lack, miss, stand in need of

grc:verb:ὁρᾶσθαι.gloss: contracted present mediopassive infinitive of ὁράω (horáō)

grc:adv:ἔπειτ'.gloss: apocopic form of ἔπειτα (épeita) (used before a smooth breathing)

grc:prep:ἐφ'.gloss: apocopic form of ἐπί (epí) (used before the rough breathing)

grc:prep:ἀφ'.gloss: apocopic form of ᾰ̓πό (ăpó) used before vowel with rough breathing

grc:verb:βλέπω.gloss: see, have the power of sight

grc:pron:τι.gloss: neuter nominative/accusative singular of τις (tis): something

grc:pron:αἱ.gloss: feminine nominative plural of ὁ (ho, demonstrative pronoun)

grc:verb:ἀφίστημι.gloss: put away, remove, keep out of the way

grc:name:Πάν.gloss: Pan, the Greek god of shepherds and nature

grc:verb:ὁρῶνται.gloss: contracted third-person plural present mediopassive indicative of ὁράω (horáō)

grc:adv:πως.gloss: in any way, at all, by any means

grc:verb:ποιῶν.gloss: contracted present active participle of ποιέω (poiéō)

grc:adj:ὅλος.gloss: whole, entire, complete in all its parts

grc:verb:γίνομαι.gloss: Ionic, Koine, and Byzantine form of γῐ́γνομαι (gĭ́gnomai)

grc:verb:γίνεται.gloss: third-person singular present mediopassive indicative of γῑ́νομαι (gī́nomai)

grc:verb:ἐγένετο.gloss: third-person singular aorist middle indicative of γίγνομαι (gígnomai)

grc:other:σ.gloss: Lower-case sigma (σίγμα), the 18th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the voiceless alveolar fricative /s/. It is preceded by ρ and followed by τ.

grc:other:ς.gloss: The lower case letter sigma of the Ancient Greek alphabet when used as the final letter in a word (a final sigma). In all other positions in a word the normal sigma (σ (s)) is used.

grc:verb:πιστεύω.gloss: trust, put faith in, rely on

grc:verb:δείκνυται.gloss: third-person singular present mediopassive indicative of δείκνῡμῐ (deíknūmĭ)

grc:noun:ἐπίπεδος.gloss: on the ground, on the ground-floor

grc:verb:ἔστω.gloss: third-person singular present active imperative of εἰμί (eimí): let her/him/it be!

grc:other:θ.gloss: Lower-case theta (θῆτα), the 8th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the voiceless aspirated dental or alveolar plosive /tʰ/ and later the voiceless dental fricative /θ/. It is preceded by η and followed by ι.

grc:other:Θ.gloss: The letter theta (θῆτα), the eighth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:conj:θ'.gloss: apocopic form of τε (te) (used before a rough breathing)

grc:other:Κ.gloss: The letter kappa (κάππα), the tenth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:part:κ'.gloss: apocopic form of κε (ke) (used before the smooth breathing)

grc:part:χ'.gloss: apocopic form of κε (ke) (used before the rough breathing)

grc:verb:ἐπιψαύω.gloss: touch on the surface, touch lightly

grc:other:Ν.gloss: The letter nu (νῦ), the 13th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:ν.gloss: Lower-case nu (νῦ), the 13th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the alveolar nasal /n/. It is preceded by μ and followed by ξ.

grc:other:χ.gloss: Lower-case chi (χεῖ), the 22nd letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the voiceless aspirated velar plosive /kʰ/ and later the voiceless velar fricative /x/. It is preceded by φ (ph) and followed by ψ (ps).

grc:other:Χ.gloss: The letter chi (χεῖ), the 22nd letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:ρ.gloss: Lower-case rho (ῥῶ), the 17th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the alveolar trill /r/. It is preceded by π and followed by σ.

grc:other:Ρ.gloss: The letter rho (ῥῶ), the 17th letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:verb:εἷμαι.gloss: first-person singular perfect mediopassive indicative of ἕζομαι (hézomai)

grc:other:α.gloss: Lower-case alpha (ἄλφα), the first letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the open front or central unrounded vowel /a/. It is followed by β.

grc:other:Α.gloss: The letter ἄλφα (álpha, “alpha”), the first letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:Β.gloss: The letter beta (βῆτα), the second letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:β.gloss: Lower-case beta (βῆτα), the second letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. It represented the voiced bilabial plosive: /b/ and later the voiced labiodental fricative /v/. It is preceded by α and followed by γ.

grc:other:ζ.gloss: Lower-case zeta, the seventh letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. Its name was ζῆτα. The sound it represented is disputed, some claim it was /zd/, others claim it was /dz/. It is preceded by ϝ and followed by η.

grc:other:Ζ.gloss: The letter zeta (ζῆτα), the sixth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:adj:τριπλάσιος.gloss: thrice as many, thrice as much, thrice as great as

grc:verb:ἔχοι.gloss: third-person singular present active optative of ἔχω (ékhō)

grc:num:δυῶν.gloss: masculine/feminine/neuter genitive plural of δῠ́ο (dŭ́o) and δῠ́ω (dŭ́ō)

grc:adj:ἅτερος.gloss: ἅτερος [a^] , Dor. etc. for ἕτερος, (Corc.); Aeol. ἄτερος , al., etc.; τὸ ἅτερον, Megarian in .

grc:verb:εἴη.gloss: third-person singular present active optative of εἰμῐ́ (eimĭ́)

grc:verb:διαιρέω.gloss: take apart, cleave in twain, divide

grc:conj:εἴ.gloss: accented form of εἰ (ei), used when followed by an unaccented enclitic

grc:verb:ἀναλαμβάνω.gloss: take up, take into one's hands

grc:noun:ὀνόματα.gloss: nominative accusative and vocative plural of ὄνομᾰ (ónomă)

grc:verb:παραδίδωμι.gloss: give, hand over to another, transmit

grc:verb:ἔστε.gloss: up to the time that, until

grc:verb:ἔστων.gloss: third-person dual present active imperative of εἰμί (eimí)

grc:noun:περίοδος.gloss: one who goes the rounds, patrol

grc:adv:ἑξῆς.gloss: one after another, in order, in a row

grc:verb:εἴρηται.gloss: third-person singular present middle subjunctive of εἴρω (eírō)

grc:other:ε.gloss: Lower case epsilon, the fifth letter of the ancient and modern Greek alphabets. Its name was εἶ, later ἒ ψιλόν (è psilón), and presently έψιλον (épsilon). It represents roughly the same sound in both alphabets: in Modern Greek, a somewhat lowered variant of the mid front unrounded vowel: /e/ or /e̞/. It is preceded by δ (d) and followed in the archaic alphabet by ϝ (w) and in the classical alphabet by ζ (z).

grc:other:Ε.gloss: The letter now called epsilon (ἒ ψιλόν (è psilón)), the fifth letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:other:η.gloss: Lower-case eta, the seventh letter of the ancient Greek alphabet. Its name was ἦτα and it represented a long open-mid front unrounded vowel: /ɛː/. It is often transliterated as either e or i. It is preceded by ζ and followed by θ.

grc:other:Η.gloss: The letter eta (ἦτα), the seventh letter of the ancient Greek alphabet.

grc:verb:χωρέω.gloss: make room for another, give way, withdraw

grc:pron:οἵ.gloss: masculine nominative plural of ὅ (hó, relative pronoun)

grc:verb:ᾠήθην.gloss: first-person singular aorist passive indicative of οἴομαι (oíomai)
